first_frame: A stylized, glowing blue/red 3D animation of a crowd of people on an escalator.
beats: 0-3 s: Hook: Visual of the escalator incident with a dramatic, stylized filter.
3-26 s: 3D Animation: Explaining the mechanics of the motor and the primary brake system.
26-42 s: Talking Head: Derek explains the failure and the test results.
42-59 s: 3D Animation: Explaining the auxiliary brake system.
59-78 s: Talking Head + Reveal: The shocking discovery of the zip-tied brake wedge.
visual_techniques: Stylized filter on stock footage (0-3 s)
Talking head with soft-focus background (26-42 s, 59-78 s)
captions: White text, 3-6 words per chunk, centered, no highlight colour.
sound: Clear, professional voiceover; subtle, tense, low-frequency atmospheric music; crisp mechanical sound effects (clamping, whirring).
recurring_element: The 3D model of the escalator motor mechanism.
ending: Punchline/Reveal: The visual proof of the zip-tied brake, followed by a hard cut to black.
why: It combines high-stakes storytelling with high-quality 3D visuals. The 'mystery' structure (how did it fail? -> oh, it was sabotaged) keeps retention high, and the visual reveal at the end provides a satisfying payoff.
reusable_faceless: Using stylized filters on stock footage for dramatic effect
3D cross-section animations to explain complex mechanical failures
The 'mystery reveal' structure where the cause of the failure is hidden until the end
Using simple graphic overlays (like a red circle) to draw attention to small details in footage
